lessons: The failure was the review reply, not the authored work. The review approved the seed and both Verification commands passed (14 and 1498 tests). Leave tests/test_seeded_phase3_12.py (commit 6b326bc) and both seeds byte-for-byte unchanged.

Why the reply failed: the requisition reviewer wrote prose before its JSON. requisition.py:129 checks the reply with RequisitionReply.model_validate_json(unwrap_fence(text)), and unwrap_fence only removes one surrounding code fence, so any prose before the JSON breaks the parse.

Re-run only the requisition review and send back exactly one JSON object with nothing before or after it: verdict, summary and findings, no other keys (extra='forbid'). If the verdict is approve, findings must be [] (requisition.py:32).

Preserve approved seeds while their bytes still match ticket_sha. Do not re-author phase3-continue-13 (sha256 184e2b95...) or kill-cli-activation unless a review returns a real snag finding. A schema error says nothing about what the ticket contains.
Leave tickets/kill-cli-activation/ and tickets/phase3-continue-13/ uncommitted so Check can record both approvals in checks.json and lift them together in one chupa(phase3-continue-12): seeds commit.
